subject: assembling the people who apparently didn’t say the things in my memories
excerpt: the answer to your question of why it is better to buy than compete is network effects. This decision doesn’t reflect a lack of confidence in our product or anything like that. It’s just that once someone has saturated a demographic somewhere, it’s harder to compete with them. We see this even when the incumbent’s product is way less efficient than our own.
context: Zuckerberg explained a 2008 acquisition to colleagues; Meta says the email concerned a company in Germany.

excerpt: Once someone wins at a specific mechanic, it’s difficult for others to supplant them without doing something different.
